text.p: The Togo government unveiled a 1997 budget foreseeing a deficit of about 10 billion CFA francs ($19.2 million) to be financed from external sources.

The shortfall is less than half the 22 billion CFA forecast in the 1996 budget, but Prime Minister Kwassi Klutse said the outgoing year's final deficit would in fact be only 700 million CFA thanks to prudent management.

"The lower deficit budgeted shows the government's willingness to apply a prudent and rigorous budgetary policy leading to a reduction of macro-economic disequilibrium and to clean up public finances," he said in his budget address.
Revenue in the 1997 year beginning January 1 is forecast at 126.2 billion CFA and spending at 136.4 billion CFA.
The government intends to broaden its revenue base and adopt the uniform Value Added Tax regime agreed by the UEMOA franc-zone monetary bloc grouping Togo and six other regional states.

The minister said final figures for 1996 would show revenue at 106.2 billion and spending at 106.8 billion CFA. The financing gap of 700 million CFA could be closed by further belt-tightening in the remaining weeks of the year, he added.
